# Papered v0.2.2 — Fast, bounded health cleanup (Alpha)

> **⚠️ Alpha Notice**
> This is an early, experimental release. The API, CLI, data format, and database schema are subject to breaking changes without notice. Not recommended for production use.

This release fixes a severe performance and memory problem in the Health → Clean up action: cleanup could pin one CPU core at 100% for 10+ minutes while RSS climbed past 1 GB, making the daemon appear hung. Cleanup is now near-instant, and the database-level operations that caused the blowup are either batched or decoupled into explicit actions.

## Fixes

- **Clean up KB is now near-instant** — Papers were deleted one statement at a time; each cascade (chunks, translations, FTS) committed the tantivy index separately, and on a fragmented index each commit cost about a second. Cleanup now collects stale paper ids first (also fixing rows skipped by OFFSET pagination while deleting) and deletes them in batches of 500 with a single `DELETE ... IN (...)` statement — one index commit per batch instead of one per paper. Measured on a 521-paper library: **12 minutes → 0.3 seconds**, with no memory spike.
- **Cleanup no longer runs `OPTIMIZE INDEX`** — The tail of cleanup triggered a full tantivy FTS segment merge (all segments of all full-text indexes merged into one), which is the actual source of the multi-minute 100% CPU and >1 GB RSS. That operation belongs to the explicit **Optimize store** button / `POST /api/v1/health/optimize`, which is unchanged and can now be run deliberately, at a convenient time. After this change, running it on an already-merged index completes in seconds.
- **Batched delete API** — New `delete_papers()` store method used by cleanup. The Turso implementation deliberately avoids an explicit transaction: libsql's FTS drop hook panics on cascade flushes inside manual transactions (turso_core 0.7.2), so deletes run as single-statement batches, which is also the production-proven path.

## Notes

- A leftover multi-hundred-MB WAL from previous sessions is checkpointed automatically on the daemon's next write; the main database file was verified to contain no dead pages (`freelist_count = 0`), so a full `VACUUM` is not needed.
